newsitem.title: USA: Dove gets $3 mln investment from group.
newsitem.headline: Dove gets $3 mln investment from group.

text.p: Dove Entertainment Inc said Wednesday that a partnership of former entertainment executives, called Media Equities International, has agreed to make an investment of $3 million in newly issued Dove shares.

The company said Media's five principals would help Dove's management address future operational and financial issues and would receive a warrant to make additional investments at increasing levels above current market.
Media is a new investment group that includes Apollo Partners principals Terence Elks and Ken Gorman, H.A.M. Media Group principals John Healy and Bruce Maggin, and media investor Ron Lightstone.
Dove's president and chief executive, Michael Viner, said Media's involvement will help accelerate the growth of the company.
"We look forward to their contributions as we continue to exploit our leadership position in audio books and extend our television production efforts," Viner said.
Elks and Healy will join Dove's board of directors while Gorman and Maggin will serve on the audit committee. Lightstone will advise in Dove's executive committee, the company said.
The transaction, expected to close on or about March 14, is subject to definitive documentation and other provisions.
